about: Read, then edit, in one turn. The user does not say 'read your configuration first'; they
describe a change that cannot be made without looking, because the anchor text has to come
from what is stored rather than from what the model remembers.
`multi-01` is the deletion case, which is where a model that skips the read is easiest to
catch: {{TOKEN}} lives in the section being removed, so its absence proves the removal, and
the surviving sections prove the rest of the document was left alone.

scenarios.title: look at the instructions, then remove one section

turns.prompt: have a look at my instructions and drop the escalation section — we track that somewhere else now.

scenarios.prompt_note: The instructions are rendered into the workspace, so the model may act without a read_config call and still be right. The verdict is therefore the stored row: the escalation token gone, every other section intact. See scenarios/01-read.json for why no read is required.

scenarios.title: two unrelated changes in one message
scenarios.prompt_note: Two commits is a legitimate answer, so the budget allows it; what it does not allow is an error.

turns.prompt: two things: drop the context7 mcp server, and in my instructions swap 'Do not use emojis.' for 'Use plain language.'

scenarios.unsupported_reason: The Pi harness rejects user MCP servers outright ("User MCPs are not supported on the Pi harness"), so the run fails before the model sees the task. Counting that as a config-editing failure would be measuring the wrong thing.
